    Finasteride vs minoxidil: what the trials show and what clinics charge.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 8 Nov 2026.

    Short answer

    Finasteride (a tablet, on a prescription) and minoxidil (on the scalp, without a prescription) are the two FDA-approved medicines for male pattern hair loss.12 In two one-year trials in 1,553 men, finasteride raised hair counts above placebo, while men on placebo kept losing hair.3 In a 48-week trial in 393 men, 5% minoxidil beat 2% minoxidil and placebo on hair counts.4 Neither is a peptide. At the online clinics we track, hair plans start at $25 a month (Strut Health, Oral Finasteride).5

    What are finasteride and minoxidil?

    Finasteride is a tablet. It blocks the body from making a male hormone in the scalp that stops hair growth. It is only for use in men.1 In our database: an FDA-approved product exists.6

    Minoxidil is a liquid or foam put on the scalp. It is meant to grow hair and slow balding, and works best in people under 40 whose hair loss is recent; it has no effect on a receding hairline.2 In our database: an FDA-approved product exists.7

    Neither one is a peptide. They are small-molecule medicines, and they are here because they are what a peptide sold for hair has to be compared with. Our hair page puts them next to the peptides sold for hair.

    What did the finasteride trials show?

    In two trials of one year, 1,553 men aged 18 to 41 with male pattern hair loss took finasteride or a placebo; 1,215 of them went on for a second year.3

    The researchers counted hairs in a circle one inch across on the crown, where the men started with about 876 hairs. Men on finasteride had 107 more hairs than men on placebo after one year and 138 more after two. Men on placebo kept losing hair. The men's own ratings, the doctors' ratings and photos all pointed the same way.3

    What did the minoxidil trial show?

    In a 48-week trial, 393 men aged 18 to 49 used 5% minoxidil, 2% minoxidil or a placebo liquid. The 5% solution did better than both on hair counts and on how the men and the doctors rated scalp coverage, and it worked sooner than the 2% one.4 Itching and irritation of the scalp were more common with the 5% solution.4

    What do they not do?

    • Both work only while you use them. Hair that grew back on finasteride is likely lost within 12 months of stopping;1 most new hair from minoxidil is lost within a few months.2
    • Both take months. Finasteride may take at least 3 months to show; if 12 months show nothing, more probably will not help.1
    • Finasteride can lower sexual desire and cause erection and ejaculation problems, during and after treatment. Women who are or may become pregnant should not touch broken tablets.1

    Which one should you use?

    That is a question for a prescriber, who will ask about your hair loss, your health and whether you plan children. Some people use both. Our comparison page puts finasteride and minoxidil side by side, with their FDA status, and our guide Peptides for hair loss shows what the peptides sold for hair have behind them. Every substance has its own page under Peptides A to Z.

    We do not give doses. None of this is medical advice.
